subject.title: fix(mxc): bound sandbox policy file reads to prevent OOM

question: Should MXC make a 1 MiB maximum size an enforced compatibility contract for already-configured sandbox policy files?
rationale: The branch deliberately converts previously unbounded operator-supplied policy files into load failures above the cap; the appropriate upgrade behavior is a sandbox-security policy choice, not something tests can infer.

options.title: Adopt the 1 MiB cap with proof
options.body: Accept the bounded-read policy, add redacted real MXC configuration-path evidence for both within-cap success and over-cap rejection, and make the failure actionable for operators.

options.title: Choose a different compatibility policy
options.body: Keep the OOM protection but choose and document another supported limit or migration behavior for existing oversized policy files.

recommendation.title: Adopt the 1 MiB cap with proof
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded-read policy, add redacted real MXC configuration-path evidence for both within-cap success and over-cap rejection, and make the failure actionable for operators.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature-history ownership could not be attributed reliably from the available read-only context; the MXC plugin and sandbox-security reviewers should jointly decide the compatibility contract.
